stem.en: Why does the popular idea that 'low blood oxygen is what makes you breathe harder' get normal respiratory physiology backward?
stem.et: Miks pöörab populaarne idee, et 'madal vere hapnikusisaldus paneb sind kõvemini hingama', normaalse hingamisfüsioloogia ümber?

label.en: Central chemoreceptors responding to rising carbon dioxide provide the dominant, moment-to-moment drive to breathe under normal conditions; peripheral chemoreceptors responding to oxygen only take over as the dominant drive once oxygen has fallen to a fairly low level.
label.et: Kesksed kemoretseptorid, mis reageerivad tõusvale süsihappegaasile, annavad normaalsetes tingimustes domineeriva, hetkelise hingamistungi; hapnikule reageerivad perifeersed kemoretseptorid võtavad domineeriva tungi üle alles siis, kui hapnik on langenud üsna madalale tasemele.

label.en: It doesn't need distinguishing from sleep apnea's mechanism anyway, since obstructive and central sleep apnea are really just one disorder with a single underlying cause.
label.et: Seda ei ole vaja eristada uneapnoe mehhanismist niikuinii, kuna obstruktiivne ja tsentraalne uneapnoe on tegelikult vaid üks häire ühe aluseks oleva põhjusega.

label.en: It doesn't get anything backward — obstructive sleep apnea shows that the brain's breathing control center itself is what typically malfunctions when breathing is disrupted.
label.et: See ei pööra midagi ümber -- obstruktiivne uneapnoe näitab, et ajus asuv hingamise kontrollikeskus ise on see, mis tavaliselt hingamise häirimisel valesti töötab.

label.en: Oxygen actually is the dominant, moment-to-moment trigger, so the popular idea is correct as stated.
label.et: Hapnik on tegelikult domineeriv, hetkeline stiimul, mistõttu populaarne idee on nii nagu öeldud õige.
